messages.author: 92c1f4710b7f5e5b
messages.subject: Complex design with time-course
parts:
Hi all,

I received a dataset from a collaborator asking for some stats, but it contains a complex experimental design, and I am wondering if MSstats can handle it.

Cells were collected from patients and submitted to three approaches: untreated (control), treatment A, and treatment B. Each approach was harvested in 3 time points: 2 hrs, 6 hrs, and 24 hrs. Lastly, cells and their media were collected and submitted to a label-free DDA approach. The total of patients was only 2.

Here is a photo of the design for one of the patients:


The collaborator wants to make some comparisons, e.g., across time and among treatments. In my little experience, this experiment seems heavily underpowered for such a complex design. However, I feel bad for not even trying so this is my attempt.

The total is 36 samples. As we have only two biological replicates, I made the annotation file with 18 samples as "1" and 18 samples as "2" in the "BioReplicate" column. Then I wrote an entire description of each sample into a single text in the "Conditions" column. For example: "Cell.TreatA.2hrs". The annotation file is attached.

When running MSstats, the FittedModels are "lm(formula = ABUNDANCE ~ GROUP, data = input)", which does not account for any paired comparisons.

Are there any extra columns that I would be able to add to pass extra information to MSstats? Or should I use another method other than MSstats?

Best,
Luiz

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: Complex design with time-course
parts:
Hi Luiz,

From the picture of the design, it looks like each patient has both cells and media. However the annotation file that you provided lists all media as replicate 1, and all cells as replicate 2. This does not correspond to your picture. Check that the BioReplicate column matches the patient id.

Thank you for using MSstats
Olga

This is more of a statistical question, but shouldn't the model include something like this: (1 | TIME.POINT)?

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: Complex design with time-course
parts:
Hi Luiz,

The GROUP variable already contains time points, if 'Condition' is constructed as you described, e.g. '"Cell.TreatA.2hrs". You can compare any subsets of conditions (such as times) using a contrast.

HTH
Olga
